_comment: Speech-to-text through the Whisper MCP server of mcp/whisper, declared in a settings file. The launcher does the same with no file to edit when ORKEON_CODE_AUDIO_DIR is set (tool and source modes): use this fragment only to declare the server yourself, for instance with another backend. Merge the Orkeon:FileSystem:Mounts entries and the MCP section into config/appsettings.local.json, then replace /home/me/audio (your audio and video files, seen by the agents as /audio), /home/me/transcripts (where the server writes, seen as /transcripts), /home/me/.local/bin/uv (the full path of uv: the REPL starts it without a shell) and /home/me/orkeon-code (this checkout). Each folder appears twice, in a mount and in Env, and the two must match. Both must exist before the REPL starts (mkdir -p them): nothing creates them. Before the first REPL, resolve the server's environment once outside it (bash scripts/whisper-mcp-smoke.sh with the same WHISPER_DEVICE, or Command and Args run by hand with < /dev/null): the REPL gives a server 30 s to answer, and the first uv run takes minutes. WHISPER_MODEL takes tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3 or turbo; the other WHISPER_* variables (backend, device, endpoint) are in mcp/whisper/README.md. A key never goes in this file: WHISPER_API_KEY_VAR names the variable that holds it. With this declaration the launcher leaves ORKEON_CODE_AUDIO_DIR and ORKEON_CODE_VOICE aside: for /say add "--extra", "tts" to Args before the script, for /voice "--extra", "voice" too, with WHISPER_MICROPHONE and WHISPER_SPEAKER at "1" in Env. Then, in the REPL: /config set tools.extra transcribe_audio:read,list_audio:read,whisper_info:read
